items.title: Westbound Hwy. 403 closed in Mississauga due to 3-vehicle crash
items.summary: The westbound lanes of Highway 403 are closed in Mississauga for a collision involving three vehicles, Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) say. Emergency services are on the scene and at least two people have suffered serious injuries in the crash. The highway is closed between Mavis Road and Erin Mills Parkway and traffic delays are expected in the area. It’s unclear how long the closure will last.

items.title: Raptors championship coach fighting Ontario over $700,000 tied to Mississauga home
items.summary: Former Toronto Raptors head coach Nick Nurse is taking legal action against the Ontario government over a denied tax refund approaching $700,000 tied to a home he and his wife previously owned in Mississauga. Nurse, who currently serves as the head coach for the Philadelphia 76ers, filed a notice of appeal with the Ontario Superior Court. 65-million property purchase in 2021. The legal battle focuses on whether the couple met the criteria for a tax rebate under the provincial regulations active at the time of their purchase. In 2021, the NRST rate for qualifying foreign buyers within the Greater Golden Horseshoe region was set at 15 per cent, a figure that the province has since raised to 25 per cent. Under those older regulations, foreign buyers could secure a rebate if they fulfilled several conditions. These parameters included maintaining continuous employment in Ontario for at least one full year and utilizing the property as a primary residence for a minimum of 60 days. Property records show the Nurses acquired the Mississauga residence in October 2021 and subsequently sold it in September 2023. The sale occurred shortly after Nurse’s ten-year tenure with the Toronto Raptors organization reached its conclusion. The Raptors parted ways with Nurse in April 2023, and he was appointed head coach of the 76ers the following month. The couple formally submitted their NRST rebate application in March 2024, which the Ministry of Finance ultimately denied. According to court documents, the ministry rejected the claim on the grounds that the Nurses were no longer residing in the Mississauga home when the application was filed. The Nurses’ appeal contests this interpretation, arguing that the regulations in effect in 2021 did not legally mandate ongoing residency at the exact time of submission.

items.title: Popular restaurant shut down after failing health inspection in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga restaurant was forced to shut down following a recent health inspection. Daal Roti Indian Tadka House, located at 6990 Financial Dr, was inspected and closed on Monday, August 10. The report from Peel Public Health alleges that the restaurant did not properly store food to prevent contamination and/or adulteration, and did not take adequate measures to prevent pests, among other health violations. The restaurant is closed and may reopen after passing a follow-up inspection. This is the only red card on the restaurant’s public record, which shows inspections going back to December 2024. Red cards are issued when an inspector finds a health risk or danger, and the establishment or service is closed until the risks are removed. A yellow conditional pass means the establishment is not following all the requirements under the Health Protection and Promotion Act, and issues that pose a risk of illness must be corrected at the time of inspection. items.title: Great Outdoors Comedy Festival brings top comedians to Mississauga’s Erindale Park
items.summary: Get ready for a weekend of laughter under the open sky as Visit Mississauga welcomes top stand-up comedians. Laughter is taking centre stage this September as the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival makes its Mississauga debut at Erindale Park from September 11 to 13. Emmy-winning and acclaimed comedians, including John Mulaney, Hasan Minhaj and Ms. Pat, will headline a weekend of live stand-up comedy alongside local food vendors and licensed beverage areas set against the scenic backdrop of the Credit River. The Great Outdoors Comedy Festival is the newest addition to Visit Mississauga‘s growing portfolio of major events. The festival brings internationally recognized comedians to the city as part of North America’s premier outdoor comedy festival. Produced by Trixstar Entertainment, the festival has grown quickly since its 2021 debut. It has featured some of the biggest names in comedy, including Jerry Seinfeld, Kevin Hart, Bill Burr, John Mulaney, Chelsea Handler, Nikki Glaser, Shane Gillis, Nate Bargatze, Amy Schumer, Theo Von, Tom Segura, Whitney Cummings, Martin Short, Matt Rife and Andrew Schulz. As the final stop on the festival’s 2026 North American tour, the Mississauga event is expected to draw thousands of visitors each day from across the Greater Toronto Area, Ontario and from communities throughout Ontario and Canada. Combining headline comedy performances with food, beverages and a vibrant outdoor atmosphere, the festival offers visitors another great reason to spend the weekend exploring Mississauga while supporting local hotels, restaurants and businesses. The lineup for the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival in Mississauga includes five headliners and a talented supporting cast. Check out the video for a peek at the festival lineup. Find out more about the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival comedians. The Great Outdoors Comedy Festival is Canada’s premier outdoor comedy festival, bringing world-class stand-up comedy to iconic outdoor venues across the country.

items.title: Heartland Town Centre Adds a Leather Brand, a Global Retailer and a Ramen Spot in 2026
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's Heartland Town Centre at Mavis Road and Britannia Road has picked up a string of new tenants during the first half of 2026. Canadian leather brand Danier, founded in 1972, opened its Heartland location in March, bringing its selection of leather jackets, bags, boots, wallets and accessories to the outdoor shopping centre. INsauga reports Danier has built its reputation over more than 40 years on high-quality leathers and materials. International retailer Miniso opened at Heartland in June, offering beauty products, home decor, electronics, toys, stationery and snacks at affordable prices. INsauga notes Miniso operates more than 5,000 locations worldwide and has run collaborations with brands including Coca-Cola, Marvel, Hello Kitty, Sesame Street and the Beijing Palace Museum. Kinton Ramen has also become one of the shopping centre's most popular stops, serving ramen built on rich broths, signature noodles and a variety of fresh toppings. INsauga says more openings are expected at Heartland before the end of the year.

items.title: Crews Finish the Eastern Tunnels That Will Link Scarborough and Mississauga on One Transit Line
items.summary: According to INsauga, crews have completed excavation of the eastern underground segment of the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension, digging twin 500-metre tunnels between Mount Dennis Station and Jane Street. Metrolinx, the provincial agency building the line, says it will operate mainly underground and eventually connect to the already-completed western underground segment, which finished tunnelling back in 2024. At Jane Street, trains will surface onto an elevated guideway running to Scarlett Road before dropping back underground into that western portion of the route. Ontario's transportation minister, Prabmeet Sarkaria, said in a statement that the extension will make it faster and easier for thousands of commuters to get where they're going each day, while also improving connectivity across the GTA and supporting thousands of construction jobs. INsauga reports that once finished, the project will extend Line 5 Eglinton further west, creating nearly 30 kilometres of continuous rapid transit along Eglinton Avenue linking Scarborough, midtown Toronto and Mississauga.

items.title: Peel Highways Brace for 32 Scheduled Closures on Aug. 11
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the province has scheduled 32 separate closures across provincial highways in Peel Region for August 11, 2026. The affected routes include Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410, Highway 9 and the Queen Elizabeth Way, the same corridors that carry most commuter and commercial traffic through Mississauga and the surrounding region. Mississauga.com advises drivers to plan their route before heading out given how many highways are affected at once. The outlet's listing does not spell out a reason for this particular round of closures, though its coverage of other recent days has tied similar work to short-term repairs and routine highway maintenance. Anyone driving through Peel this week should build extra time into their trip and watch for detours. Mississauga.com also points readers to a separate closure list for anyone travelling to highways outside Peel Region.

items.title: Citing overcrowding, Mississauga animal services runs $25 adoption blitz
items.summary: In an effort to ease overcrowding, Mississauga Animal Services Shelter says it's running a $25 dog and cat adoption blitz until the end of August.

items.title: A Wrong-Way Turn on the QEW Turns Fatal for an 83-Year-Old Hanover Woman
items.summary: According to Ontario Provincial Police, an 83-year-old woman from Hanover has died after she drove the wrong way into oncoming traffic on the Queen Elizabeth Way in Mississauga. Mississauga.com reports the crash happened near Erin Mills Parkway on the night of Aug. 7, when the woman's sedan, travelling toward Toronto in the Fort Erie-bound lanes, collided head-on with another vehicle. Police at the scene initially believed both drivers had suffered only minor injuries. According to OPP, the wrong-way driver's injuries were later upgraded to life-threatening, and she died in hospital. Mississauga.com reports the crash remains under investigation. OPP is asking anyone with information or video footage of the incident to call 1-888-310-1122.

items.title: How a New Rapid-Assessment Clinic Diagnosed a Mississauga Mom's Skin Cancer in Two Weeks After Others Missed It
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Mississauga mother of three Liliya Leheta had her skin cancer symptoms dismissed by dermatologists for nearly two years before a new rapid assessment clinic at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre diagnosed her within two weeks of her referral. The Star reports Leheta first noticed her skin peeling on her chest in March 2023 after a day out with her kids without sunscreen, and later found a small red mole near the centre of her chest that she initially dismissed. Over the following two years, she watched the mole swell, change shape and bleed, all while an earlier referral to a specialist had been declined. In the fall of 2025, Leheta learned about the newly opened rapid assessment centre for skin cancer at Princess Margaret and was seen within two weeks of being referred there. She was diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma, the most common form of skin cancer in Canada, and a surgeon successfully removed the cancerous tissue less than two months later. The Star reports Leheta remains cancer-free today.
